text:
The Blues are in the middle of a retool, and the clearest sign of it is in goal. Joel Hofer has taken the starting job, and he is earning it: a .932 save percentage and 4.8 goals saved above expected over his last five starts (3-2-0). Jordan Binnington, the goalie who won St. Louis its 2019 Stanley Cup, has made only five appearances and is in the last year of his contract, and Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman has reported trade noise around him.

At 9-8-2 and 20 points, Jim Montgomery's team is exactly what its chances say it is (about 20 points' worth, per our numbers). The Blues have 48.6% of the expected goals (the quality of chances for and against). Hofer's saves have covered for an attack that has scored more than five goals fewer than its chances predicted, and that finishing gap is the part most likely to improve.

The newer faces are carrying some of the load. Jimmy Snuggerud keeps producing on the top line with Robert Thomas and Dylan Holloway, and Mason McTavish and Connor McMichael anchor a second line that creates more than it allows. Justin Barron (9 points in 10, against 3.8 expected) is running well ahead of his chances. Logan Mailloux finally made his season debut this week after a broken hand.

The Blues are disciplined, at about three minors a game. Our numbers give them a 35% chance at the playoffs. Where Binnington ends up will say plenty about the plan.
headline: Hofer takes the net as the Blues retool
